High-level answers / clarifications:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted control plane and inference runtime; attached is the most recent report (redacted). For deeper evidence we can initiate an NDA and provide an access bundle.

- Logs & backups: Default log retention is 90 days; backups (immutable snapshots) are retained 180 days by default. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate shorter retention windows for backups where feasible, or implement additional controls for deletion-on-demand where required.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support data processing agreements and will sign reasonable provisions; we also offer Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) where Amaya needs physical control.

Hi Jacob & team,

Thanks — received the questionnaire (attached to this thread). Neha and I reviewed and put together initial answers inline in the questionnaire and a short SLA table (attached). Summary answers to your numbered items below: 

1) Backups vs physical deletion: Our standard process treats snapshots as separate from live-store deletion. By default, immutable backups are retained for 180 days. Physical deletion from live stores completes within 30 days, but snapshots may retain content until their retention expiry. For enterprise agreements, we can negotiate snapshot retention or implement accelerated purge workflows where technically feasible; note that some storage providers impose minimum retention for snapshots.

2) Logs vs customer content: Logs (audit/forensics) are retained separately and the default retention is 90 days. If Amaya needs 1-year audit log retention we can provide extended retention for logs as an add-on; that does not change customer content deletion timelines unless otherwise contracted.

3) Customer-managed keys: Yes — for hosted deployments we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. For private deployments we can provide HSM integrations.

4) Questionnaire: Neha has completed the technical sections and flagged a few items for Rishi/legal (answers that require contractual language or SOC 2 artifact references). Hi Jacob / Sophie — following up with the requested technical clarifications. Short version first, then a few implementation notes.

Short answers:
- Deletion propagation: when a customer issues a delete, we mark the objects for logical deletion immediately and purge from live-serving stores within 24 hours. Physical deletion from object storage is completed as part of our garbage collection cycle; SLA for full purging from live stores is 30 days.
- Backups/snapshots: immutable snapshots are retained on a separate schedule (default 180 days). Those snapshots are read-only; removing an item from a snapshot requires running an accelerated purge workflow which we currently offer as a contractual option for enterprise customers and may require coordination with the underlying cloud provider.
- Logs: audit/forensics logs are on a separate retention and indexing pipeline; default is 90 days, extended retention to 12 months is available as an add-on.
- Key management: hosted customers can bring their own KMS keys; HSM integration is available for Private deployments.

Implementation notes / caveats:
- For backups marked immutable by cloud snapshot APIs, immediate removal can be constrained by provider-level immutability guarantees; we’ll surface those constraints up front if they apply.
- Deletion of derived artifacts (search indices, cached KV entries) is handled by an internal purge pipeline; index purges typically complete within 48 hours of the logical deletion event.
- If Amaya has a legal or regulatory requirement for guaranteed removal from all retention tiers within X days, we recommend Private deployment or a contractual SLA that explicitly covers accelerated backup purges (we can scope effort and exceptions).

Happy to hop on the follow-up call and walk through the questionnaire answers live. If you want, I can also export a short architecture note showing where customer content, logs, and backups live and the purge paths.
